evals.name: references-from-artboards
evals.prompt: A designer handed over the artboards for the Checkout screen as files in {fixture}/checkout-canvas (two .dc.html artboards, canvas.json, one image). Produce the reference PNGs the screenshot parity task will compare against, into {fixture}/snapshots/design, and write the token table for the screen into {fixture}/tokens.md. Do not write any Kotlin yet; there is no Compose project here.
evals.expected_output: Checkout_Empty.png (390x844) rendered by the skill's script from the static artboard; Checkout Data flagged as not static and not presented as a reference; both PNGs looked at; a token table with the artboard's exact values mapped to Material roles.
expectations: scripts/canvas-references.mjs from the skill was run with --dir (not a hand-written renderer)
The report says Checkout Data.dc.html is not static ({{ holes }}, sc-for) and that its PNG is not a reference
The report says the stem 'Checkout Data' is sanitised to Checkout_Data and how the fixture must be named
Both rendered PNGs were opened and looked at, and the Empty one is described correctly (centred circle, 'Your cart is empty', a logo image)
tokens.md maps #f7f5f2, #b45309, #1c1917 and #57534e to theme roles rather than literals, and records 20px/600 and 14px as type roles, gap 16, radius 32, root 390x844
The report proposes the fixture as group Checkout, name Empty, width 390, height 844
The report asks for a static version of the Data artboard or a hand export, and does not edit the artboard source
The font in the artboard (system-ui) is flagged as not reproducible and a bundled family is requested

evals.name: real-canvas-single-file-four-frames
evals.prompt: The designer's canvas for a food-kiosk app was exported from claude.ai/design as files into {fixture}/design (one .dc.html with four 1080x1920 frames inside it, plus the two runtime scripts it references). The Compose project it is for is {project} (read it for its theme and existing fixtures, but do not modify it). Produce the reference PNGs the screenshot parity task will compare against, into {fixture}/snapshots/design, and write the token table plus the artboard-to-fixture mapping into {fixture}/tokens.md. Do not write Kotlin. Where the canvas cannot give a usable reference, say exactly why and what to ask the designer for.
evals.setup: a real single-file canvas (design_doc_mode canvas, several frames in one .dc.html, <image-slot> custom elements, Google Fonts, template logic in one frame) and a project with a committed design/tokens.json to grade the token table against; not bundled - point {fixture} at your own export
evals.expected_output: One reference per frame at the frame's size, named like the project's existing fixtures, with the frame's border excluded; the frame with template logic and the empty image slots flagged; the token table agreeing with the project's tokens; the project untouched.
expectations: The single file is recognised as several frames and one reference per frame is produced at 1080x1920, not one PNG of the whole page
The references are named like the project's existing fixtures (<group>_<name>.png as viddik would look them up)
The frame's 1px canvas border is excluded so the size matches the fixture exactly
The frame that carries template logic (sc-for, holes, DCLogic state) is flagged as not static and not presented as a drawn reference without saying so
Empty <image-slot> placeholders are flagged as areas that will always differ, with what to ask the designer for
The Google Fonts dependency (network at render time) and the fixture font are compared and the consequence for parity stated
The token table's colours are a subset of, or agree with, the project's committed tokens; canvas chrome colours are not presented as screen tokens
Screens the product has but the canvas does not are reported as missing references, not drawn by the agent
The project directory is not modified
No heavyweight tooling is installed to render (the skill's script or the project's own tools suffice)
